subject.name: Mathematics
subject.description: Cambridge International AS & A Level Mathematics, covering all six papers: Pure Mathematics 1, 2 and 3, Mechanics, and Probability & Statistics 1 and 2. Each paper's topics form their own section, so you can follow the papers you are taking. The questions are original practice questions written in the style of Cambridge papers, not reproduced past paper material.

topics.title: Quadratics
topics.summary: Completing the square, the discriminant, solving quadratic equations and inequalities.

topics.title: Functions
topics.summary: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, transformations of graphs.

topics.title: Coordinate geometry
topics.summary: Equations of lines and circles, intersections of lines and curves.

topics.title: Circular measure
topics.summary: Radians, arc length and sector area.

topics.title: Trigonometry
topics.summary: Graphs of trigonometric functions, exact values, identities and equations.

topics.title: Series
topics.summary: Binomial expansion, arithmetic and geometric progressions, sum to infinity.

topics.title: Differentiation
topics.summary: Gradients, the chain rule, tangents and normals, stationary points, rates of change.

topics.title: Integration
topics.summary: Integration as the reverse of differentiation, definite integrals, areas and volumes of revolution.

topics.title: Algebra
topics.summary: Modulus, polynomial division, the factor and remainder theorems.

topics.title: Logarithmic and exponential functions
topics.summary: Laws of logarithms, exponential equations, ln and e, linear forms.

topics.title: Trigonometry
topics.summary: sec, cosec, cot, identities, addition and double angle formulae, R cos(θ ± α).

topics.title: Differentiation
topics.summary: Exponentials, logarithms, trigonometric functions, product, quotient, parametric and implicit.

topics.title: Integration
topics.summary: Integrating eˣ, 1/x, trigonometric functions; the trapezium rule.

topics.title: Numerical solution of equations
topics.summary: Locating roots by sign change and iterative methods.

topics.title: Algebra
topics.summary: Modulus inequalities, binomial expansion for any rational n, partial fractions.

topics.title: Logarithmic and exponential functions
topics.summary: Solving exponential and logarithmic equations.

topics.title: Trigonometry
topics.summary: Identities, compound and double angles, R cos(θ ± α).

topics.title: Differentiation
topics.summary: Product, quotient and chain rules, parametric and implicit differentiation.

topics.title: Integration
topics.summary: Partial fractions, substitution, integration by parts.

topics.title: Numerical solution of equations
topics.summary: Iteration and convergence.

topics.title: Vectors
topics.summary: Lines in 3D, scalar product, angles, intersections and skew lines.

topics.title: Differential equations
topics.summary: Forming and solving first-order separable equations.

topics.title: Complex numbers
topics.summary: Arithmetic, modulus and argument, Argand diagrams, roots of polynomials.

topics.title: Forces and equilibrium
topics.summary: Resolving forces, friction, equilibrium of a particle.

topics.title: Kinematics of motion in a straight line
topics.summary: Displacement, velocity, acceleration, constant acceleration and calculus.

topics.title: Momentum
topics.summary: Conservation of linear momentum in collisions.

topics.title: Newton's laws of motion
topics.summary: Applying F = ma, connected particles, pulleys and lifts.

topics.title: Energy, work and power
topics.summary: Work, kinetic and potential energy, power.

topics.title: Representation of data
topics.summary: Graphs, averages, measures of spread.

topics.title: Permutations and combinations
topics.summary: Arrangements and selections.

topics.title: Probability
topics.summary: Combined events, independence, conditional probability.

topics.title: Discrete random variables
topics.summary: Probability distributions, binomial and geometric distributions.

topics.title: The normal distribution
topics.summary: Normal probabilities and the normal approximation to the binomial.

topics.title: The Poisson distribution
topics.summary: Poisson probabilities and approximations.

topics.title: Linear combinations of random variables
topics.summary: Expectation and variance of combinations.

topics.title: Continuous random variables
topics.summary: Probability density functions, mean, variance and median.

topics.title: Sampling and estimation
topics.summary: Unbiased estimates, sampling distributions, confidence intervals.

topics.title: Hypothesis tests
topics.summary: Tests using binomial, Poisson and normal distributions; errors.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Express 2x² − 12x + 7 in the form a(x + b)² + c. Give your answer in that form.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who first took out the factor of 2 from the x terms were usually successful. A common error was c = −2, from failing to multiply 9 by 2.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the set of values of k for which the equation x² + kx + 9 = 0 has no real roots. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the discriminant: k² − 36
M1 for setting k² − 36 < 0 and finding critical values ±6

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates found the critical values but then gave the incorrect region k < −6, k > 6, or used ≤.

questions.stem: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = 3x − 2 for x ∈ ℝ and g(x) = 1/(x + 1) for x > −1.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the value of fg(1).
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found gf(1) instead. fg(x) means apply g first.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find an expression for f⁻¹(x).

markingPoints.text: M1 for a correct first step, e.g. x = 3y − 2

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

questions.stem: A circle has equation x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the radius of the circle.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates completed the square correctly. Sign errors in the centre were common.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at the point (6, 2). Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for tangent gradient = −3/4 and use of (6, 2)

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should remember the tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

questions.stem: A sector OAB of a circle has centre O, radius 8 cm and angle AOB = 1.2 radians.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of the sector, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the area of the segment bounded by the arc AB and the chord AB, in cm², correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for triangle area ½ × 8² × sin 1.2
M1 for sector area − triangle area

parts.examinerComment: A significant number of candidates had their calculators in degree mode, giving sin 1.2° and an incorrect answer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve 2sin²θ − sin θ − 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for factorising: (2 sin θ + 1)(sin θ − 1) = 0
A1 for sin θ = 1 giving θ = 90°
A1 for sin θ = −1/2 giving θ = 210°
A1 for θ = 330° and no extra solutions in range

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates factorised correctly. Many lost the final mark by missing 330° or including extra solutions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of tan(π/3) − 2cos(π/6).
parts.examinerComment: Exact values should be recalled rather than found by calculator.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the coefficient of x³ in the expansion of (2 − x)⁶.
parts.examinerComment: The negative sign was frequently lost.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A geometric progression has first term 24 and common ratio 0.75. Find the sum to infinity.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

questions.stem: A curve has equation y = x³ − 6x² + 9x + 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the curve at the point where x = 4.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the stationary points and determine their nature. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using d²y/dx² = 6x − 12 or another valid method

parts.examinerComment: Candidates must give a reason for the nature of each point; stating 'maximum' without justification did not earn the final mark.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Evaluate the integral of (6x² − 4x) with respect to x, from x = 1 to x = 3.
parts.examinerComment: Arithmetic errors when substituting the lower limit were common.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The region bounded by y = √x, the x-axis and the line x = 4 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid formed, as a multiple of π. Enter the multiple only (e.g. for 5π enter 5).
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates integrated √x rather than (√x)². The volume formula requires y².

parts.prompt: Find the set of values of x for which 2x² − 5x − 3 > 0.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates found the critical values but then gave the region between them. A sketch of the parabola avoids this.

parts.prompt: The function f is defined by f(x) = (x − 2)² + 1 for x ≥ 2. Find an expression for f⁻¹(x).

markingPoints.text: M1 for swapping x and y or making x the subject
M1 for (x − 2)² = y − 1 and square rooting

parts.examinerComment: Answers with ± were not accepted: the domain x ≥ 2 means only the positive root applies.

parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line through (1, 4) that is perpendicular to the line 2x + 3y = 7. Give your answer in the form y = mx + c.

markingPoints.text: B1 for gradient of given line = −2/3
M1 for perpendicular gradient 3/2 and use of (1, 4)

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates used the gradient 2/3, forgetting the negative reciprocal.

parts.prompt: A sector of a circle has radius 5 cm and arc length 12 cm. Find the area of the sector, in cm².

markingPoints.text: M1 for angle = 12/5 = 2.4 rad, or area = ½ × r × arc length

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who first found the angle in radians usually succeeded.

parts.prompt: Prove the identity (1 − cos²θ) / (sin θ cos θ) ≡ tan θ.

markingPoints.text: A1 for simplifying sin²θ / (sin θ cos θ) = sin θ / cos θ = tan θ, with no errors

parts.examinerComment: Proofs should start from one side and work clearly to the other. Working on both sides at once is not a valid proof.

parts.prompt: An arithmetic progression has first term 7 and common difference 4. Find the sum of the first 20 terms.
parts.examinerComment: Using (n − 1)d with n = 20 was essential; some used 20d.

parts.prompt: A curve has equation y = (3x − 1)⁵. Find the gradient of the curve at the point where x = 1.
parts.examinerComment: The factor of 3 from the chain rule was frequently omitted, giving 80.

parts.prompt: Find the area of the region enclosed by the curve y = 6x − x² and the x-axis.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates needed to find where the curve meets the x-axis before integrating.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation |2x − 3| = 5.

markingPoints.text: M1 for 2x − 3 = 5 or 2x − 3 = −5 (or squaring both sides)

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found x = 4. The negative case was often forgotten.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the remainder when x³ − 4x² + x + 6 is divided by (x − 1).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered using the remainder theorem.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Given that (x + 1) is a factor of x³ + ax² − x − 2, find the value of a.

markingPoints.text: M1 for substituting x = −1 and setting equal to 0

parts.examinerComment: Sign errors when substituting −1 were the main source of lost marks.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation 3ˣ = 20, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for x ln 3 = ln 20 or equivalent

parts.examinerComment: Answers to fewer significant figures than asked lost the accuracy mark.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation ln(x + 2) − ln x = ln 3.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates wrote ln(x + 2) − ln x = ln 2, a misuse of the laws of logarithms.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: The variables x and y satisfy y = Ae^(kx). The graph of ln y against x is a straight line with gradient 0.4 and intercept 1.2 on the ln y axis. Find A, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates should state ln y = ln A + kx before comparing with the straight-line form.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Express 3 sin θ + 4 cos θ in the form R sin(θ + α), where R > 0. State the value of R.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For the expression in part (a), find α in degrees, correct to 2 decimal places, where 0° < α < 90°.
parts.examinerComment: Some used tan α = 3/4, giving 36.87°.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation 2 sec²θ − 3 tan θ − 1 = 0 for 0° < θ < 90°. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for solving: tan θ = 1 or 1/2

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who did not use the identity could make no progress.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the curve y = x²e^(3x) at the point where x = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the product rule

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates forgot the factor of 3 when differentiating e^(3x).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A curve has parametric equations x = t², y = 2t³. Find dy/dx when t = 2.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered by those who remembered to divide in the right order.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of y = ln(3x + 2) at the point where x = 1.
parts.examinerComment: The numerator 3 was often missing.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of e^(2x) from x = 0 to x = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates gave e^(2x)/2 evaluated at 1 only, forgetting the lower limit.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of the integral of 2/(2x + 1) from x = 0 to x = 1, then give it correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using limits: ln 3 − ln 1

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use the trapezium rule with 2 intervals to estimate the integral of √(1 + x²) from x = 0 to x = 2. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Using 2 intervals means h = 1. A common error was taking h = 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the equation x³ − 2x − 5 = 0 has a root between x = 2 and x = 3.

markingPoints.text: M1 for evaluating f(2) = −1 and f(3) = 16
A1 for stating the sign change, so a root lies between 2 and 3

parts.examinerComment: A conclusion referring to the change of sign is required for the second mark.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the iterative formula xₙ₊₁ = ∛(2xₙ + 5), with x₁ = 2, to find the root correct to 3 decimal places.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the iteration correctly at least once
M1 for continuing until values agree to 3 d.p.

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should show each iterate to at least 5 decimal places.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Show that the equation ln x = 3 − x has a root between x = 2 and x = 3.

markingPoints.text: M1 for considering f(x) = ln x + x − 3 and evaluating f(2) ≈ −0.31 and f(3) ≈ 1.10

parts.examinerComment: Rearranging to f(x) = 0 first makes the sign change argument clearer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Expand (1 + 2x)^(−1/2) in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x².

markingPoints.text: M1 for the binomial form with n = −1/2

parts.examinerComment: The most common error was not squaring the 2 in the x² term.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Express (5x + 1) / ((x + 1)(x − 1)) in partial fractions.

markingPoints.text: M1 for A/(x + 1) + B/(x − 1) and a method to find A or B

parts.examinerComment: Substituting x = 1 and x = −1 was the quickest method.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality |x − 2| < |2x + 1|.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who solved only x − 2 = 2x + 1 missed half the solution.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation 2^(2x) − 5(2^x) + 6 = 0.

markingPoints.text: M1 for substituting u = 2^x to get u² − 5u + 6 = 0

parts.examinerComment: Recognising the hidden quadratic is the key step.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation ln(2x − 1) = 2, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation 5^(x + 1) = 3^(2x), giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for taking logarithms: (x + 1) ln 5 = 2x ln 3

parts.examinerComment: Errors in rearranging after taking logs were common.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation cos 2θ + 3 cos θ = 1 for 0° < θ < 360°.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates should state why cos θ = −2 has no solutions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that tan A = 1/2 and tan B = 1/3, find the exact value of tan(A + B).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Express cos x − √3 sin x in the form R cos(x + α), where R > 0 and 0° < α < 90°. Give the exact values of R and α.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of y = x/(x + 1) at the point where x = 1.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the quotient rule

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The curve x² + xy + y² = 7 passes through (1, 2). Find dy/dx at this point.
parts.examinerComment: The product rule on xy was the most common source of error.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the exact coordinates of the stationary point on the curve y = xe^(−x).

markingPoints.text: M1 for product rule: e^(−x) − xe^(−x)

parts.examinerComment: Exact means leaving the answer as 1/e rather than 0.368.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of the integral of xeˣ from x = 0 to x = 1.

markingPoints.text: M1 for integrating by parts with u = x
M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: Choosing u = eˣ makes the integral harder.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of sin²x from x = 0 to x = π/2, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The double angle identity is essential here.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of 2x/(x² + 1) from x = 0 to x = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for recognising the f'(x)/f(x) form

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use the iteration xₙ₊₁ = cos xₙ, with x₁ = 0.7 and x in radians, to find the root of x = cos x correct to 3 decimal places.

markingPoints.text: M1 for at least one correct iterate

parts.examinerComment: Calculators in degree mode gave nonsense answers.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Show that the equation eˣ = 3 − x has a root between x = 0.7 and x = 0.8.

markingPoints.text: M1 for evaluating eˣ + x − 3 at both values: −0.286 and 0.026

parts.examinerComment: Values should be given to enough accuracy to show the sign.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use the iteration xₙ₊₁ = ln(3 − xₙ), with x₁ = 0.8, to find this root correct to 2 decimal places.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the angle between the vectors a = i + 2j + 2k and b = 2i − j + 2k, in degrees, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The line l has equation r = (i + 2k) + t(2i + j − k). Find the value of t for which l passes through the point (5, 2, 0).

markingPoints.text: M1 for forming an equation in t from one component
A1 for t = 2, checked in all three components

parts.examinerComment: All three components should be checked.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Lines l₁: r = (i + j) + s(i + k) and l₂: r = (2i + 3k) + t(j + k). Determine whether the lines intersect, are parallel, or are skew.

markingPoints.text: B1 for stating the directions are not parallel
M1 for equating components: 1 + s = 2, 1 = t, s = 3 + t
A1 for s = 1, t = 1 from two equations
A1 for showing the third equation fails (1 ≠ 4), so the lines are skew

parts.examinerComment: To show lines are skew, you must show they are not parallel and do not intersect.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve dy/dx = 2xy, given that y = 1 when x = 0. Find y when x = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for separating variables: ∫ 1/y dy = ∫ 2x dx
A1 for ln y = x² + c
M1 for using y = 1 at x = 0

parts.examinerComment: Missing the constant of integration made it impossible to use the initial condition.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve dy/dx = (y + 1)/x for x > 0, given that y = 1 when x = 1. Find y when x = 3.

markingPoints.text: A1 for ln(y + 1) = ln x + c

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who combined logs carefully reached y + 1 = 2x efficiently.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: The temperature θ °C of a cooling liquid decreases at a rate proportional to (θ − 20). Write down a differential equation relating θ and time t.

markingPoints.text: B1 for dθ/dt = k(θ − 20) with a constant
B1 for a negative sign or a statement that k < 0 for a decrease

parts.examinerComment: The sign of the constant must reflect that the temperature decreases.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the modulus of the complex number z = 3 + 4i.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Express (2 + i)/(1 − i) in the form x + iy.

markingPoints.text: M1 for multiplying numerator and denominator by 1 + i

parts.examinerComment: Multiplying by the conjugate of the denominator is the standard method.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation z² + 4z + 13 = 0.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the quadratic formula or completing the square

parts.examinerComment: Both roots are required.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A particle of mass 2 kg rests on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. It is held in equilibrium by a force P N acting up the plane, parallel to it. Find P.

markingPoints.text: M1 for resolving parallel to the plane: P = 2g sin 30°

parts.examinerComment: Use g = 10 m s⁻². Resolving vertically instead of along the plane was a common error.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A box of mass 5 kg rests on rough horizontal ground. The coefficient of friction is 0.4. Find the least horizontal force needed to move the box, in N.

markingPoints.text: M1 for F = μR with R = 50

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Forces of 6 N and 8 N act at right angles on a particle. Find the magnitude of the third force needed to keep it in equilibrium, in N.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A car accelerates uniformly from 5 m s⁻¹ to 25 m s⁻¹ in 8 s. Find the distance travelled, in m.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A stone is thrown vertically upwards at 15 m s⁻¹. Find its greatest height above the point of projection, in m.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates used g = 9.8; the syllabus uses g = 10.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line with velocity v = 3t² − 12t m s⁻¹ at time t s. Find the distance travelled between t = 0 and t = 2, in m.
parts.examinerComment: The displacement is −16 m; the question asks for distance, which is positive.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A particle of mass 3 kg moving at 4 m s⁻¹ collides with a particle of mass 1 kg at rest. They coalesce. Find their common speed, in m s⁻¹.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A 2 kg particle moving at 6 m s⁻¹ collides directly with a 4 kg particle moving at 1 m s⁻¹ in the opposite direction. After the collision the 2 kg particle moves at 2 m s⁻¹ in the opposite direction to its original motion. Find the speed of the 4 kg particle after the collision, in m s⁻¹.

markingPoints.text: M1 for conservation of momentum with correct signs

parts.examinerComment: Choosing a positive direction and sticking to it avoids sign errors.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: For the collision in part (a), find the loss of kinetic energy, in J.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A horizontal force of 12 N acts on a particle of mass 3 kg on a smooth horizontal surface. Find its acceleration, in m s⁻².
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A lift of mass 500 kg accelerates upwards at 0.8 m s⁻². Find the tension in the cable, in N.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates omitted the weight.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Particles of mass 3 kg and 2 kg are connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley and released from rest. Find the acceleration of the particles, in m s⁻².

markingPoints.text: M1 for an equation of motion for one particle
M1 for a second equation or the whole system: 3g − 2g = 5a

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A force of 20 N acting at 60° above the horizontal pulls a box 5 m along horizontal ground. Find the work done by the force, in J.
parts.examinerComment: Only the component in the direction of motion does work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A car's engine works at 30 kW while the car moves at a constant 25 m s⁻¹ on a level road. Find the resistance to motion, in N.
parts.examinerComment: Converting kW to W was essential.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A particle is released from rest at the top of a smooth slope of vertical height 3.2 m. Find its speed at the bottom, in m s⁻¹.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the interquartile range of the data 3, 7, 7, 9, 12, 14, 18.

markingPoints.text: B1 for lower quartile 7 and upper quartile 14

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For 10 values, Σx = 52 and Σx² = 300. Find the standard deviation, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Some forgot to square root the variance.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: In a histogram, the class 10 ≤ x < 15 has frequency 30. Find its frequency density.
parts.examinerComment: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the number of different arrangements of the letters of the word LETTER.
parts.examinerComment: Both repeated letters (E and T) must be accounted for.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A committee of 4 is chosen from 6 men and 5 women. In how many ways can it be chosen with exactly 2 women?
parts.examinerComment: Adding instead of multiplying was a common error.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: In how many ways can 7 people sit in a row if two particular people must sit next to each other?
parts.examinerComment: Treating the pair as one unit is the key idea.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Events A and B are independent, with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5. Find P(A ∪ B).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown. Find the probability that the total is 8. Give your answer as a fraction.
parts.examinerComment: A sample space diagram helps.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: P(A ∩ B) = 0.12 and P(B) = 0.3. Find P(A | B).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: X ~ B(10, 0.3). Find P(X = 2), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The probability of success in each trial is 0.2. Find the probability that the first success occurs on the 4th trial.
parts.examinerComment: This is a geometric distribution.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A random variable X takes values 1, 2 and 3 with probabilities 0.2, 0.5 and 0.3. Find E(X).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: X ~ N(50, 16). Find P(X < 56), correct to 4 decimal places.
parts.examinerComment: Dividing by the variance (16) instead of the standard deviation (4) was the most common error.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: X ~ N(μ, 25) and P(X > 60) = 0.1. Find μ, correct to 4 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: X ~ B(100, 0.4). Use a suitable normal approximation to find P(X ≥ 45), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Omitting the continuity correction lost a mark.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: X ~ Po(3). Find P(X = 2), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: X ~ Po(2.5). Find P(X ≤ 1), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Emails arrive at random at an average rate of 4 per hour. Find the probability that exactly 2 arrive in a 30-minute period, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The rate must be scaled to the time period.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: X ~ N(10, 4) and Y ~ N(15, 9) are independent. Find Var(2X − Y).
parts.examinerComment: Variances add, even when the variables are subtracted.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For the X in part (a), find E(3X + 2).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: For X and Y in part (a), find P(X + Y > 28), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: The continuous random variable X has probability density function f(x) = kx² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3, and 0 otherwise. Find k.

markingPoints.text: M1 for ∫ kx² dx from 0 to 3 = 1

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For this distribution, find E(X).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the median of X, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for ∫ from 0 to m of x²/9 dx = 0.5

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A random sample of 50 values gives Σx = 1250 and Σx² = 32 000. Find an unbiased estimate of the population variance, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Dividing by n instead of n − 1 lost marks.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A random sample of 64 values from a population with standard deviation 4 has mean 25. Find a 95% confidence interval for the population mean.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: X ~ N(80, 144). A random sample of 36 values is taken. Find the probability that the sample mean exceeds 83, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The variance of the sample mean is σ²/n.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A coin is thought to be biased towards heads. State suitable null and alternative hypotheses for a test, where p is the probability of a head.
parts.examinerComment: Hypotheses must be stated in terms of the parameter p.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The coin is thrown 20 times and shows 15 heads. Assuming H₀, find P(X ≥ 15), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Carry out the test at the 5% significance level, stating your conclusion in context.

markingPoints.text: A1 for rejecting H₀: there is evidence that the coin is biased towards heads

parts.examinerComment: Conclusions must be in context and should not be stated as certain.
